title: Early Holocene crop cultivation and landscape modification in Amazonia
version: Nature 581, pp. 190–193, DOI 10.1038/s41586-020-2162-7. Bern repository author manuscript, DOI 10.7892/boris.143456, rendered by CORE.
lineage: Original plant microfossil and dated profile study. The manuscript and published abstract are versions of one study. PDF bytes unavailable via direct download.

passages.locator: Evidence of early plant cultivation, Figs. 2–3 and Extended Data Table 2
passages.note: Isla Manechi levels yielded a heart-shaped Manihot phytolith at approximately 10,350 cal BP and scalloped squash-rind phytoliths at approximately 10,250 cal BP. Squash measurements fall within a domesticated range. Site 575 had squash at approximately 9850 cal BP.

passages.locator: Evidence of early plant cultivation and Implication for biodiversity
passages.note: The authors give probable cultivation in fertile home gardens on the islands. They do not establish an in situ origin for the squash or a prepared planting surface in the earliest sampled strata.
